svg.text: A total per key, with bounded memory — stack and heap at every step
9 events, 2 keys · allowance 295 correct, 294 gets 1 of 2 wrong · longest gap 295
1 // primitive: len(xs) — element count. len(EVENTS) = 9 · keys = 2
2 // primitive: EVENTS — what arrives, in time order. Written key@time:value.
5 // primitive: acc — one running total per key. This is the state, and it is the problem.
6 // primitive: last — when each key was last touched. Needed only to expire it.
7 // primitive: TTL — how long a key may go untouched before it is dropped.
9 // primitive: gapsOf(k) — the intervals between one key's events.
10 // longest gap per key = a:295 b:130 · worst overall = 295
11 // primitive: GONE — the key is not in the state, which is indistinguishable from new.
12 // primitive: keyOf(e) / valueOf(e) / timeOf(e) — the three fields of an event.
14 // primitive: lastTimeOf(events) — the time of the final event.
16 // primitive: maxOf(a, b) — the larger of two numbers. maxOf(2, 127) = 127
17 // primitive: remove(m, k) — drop one key from a map.
18 // remove(a map of 2, a key) = 1 entries left
19 // primitive: emptyMap() — no keys, and a missing key reads as 0.
21 // primitive: keysOf(m) — the keys a map holds.
22 // keysOf(acc) = [a, b] once both have been seen
23 // primitive: NONE — no previous event yet, so no gap can be measured.
24 // primitive: INFINITY — an allowance nothing ever exceeds, i.e. no expiry at all.
27 // "Events carry a key and a value, forever. Report a running total per key. Keys never
28 // stop arriving, so the state cannot grow without bound — bound it. What does the
29 // bound cost, and how do you choose it?"
31 // function: add(acc, e) — the whole computation. One number per key.
32 // add over all 9 events = a:24 b:21
38 // function: dropStale(acc, now) — remove any key untouched for longer than TTL. This is
39 // the only thing standing between the state and unbounded growth.
40 // at 540 with TTL = 294, "a" is dropped (last touched 245)
50 // function: onEvent(acc, e) — drop first, then add. The order is why the next frames
51 // happen: a key dropped a moment ago is indistinguishable from a key never seen.
57 // function: totals(events, ttl) — run the whole stream at one allowance.
70 // function: longestGap(events, k) — the number the allowance has to beat, and it is a
71 // property of the DATA rather than of the design.
78 if (prev != NONE) { worst = maxOf(worst, timeOf(e) - prev) }
85 // function: main() — unbounded, then two allowances.
87 val free = totals(EVENTS, INFINITY) // a:24 b:21, 2 keys held
88 val safe = totals(EVENTS, 295) // a:24 b:21, all correct
89 val tight = totals(EVENTS, 294) // a:8 b:21, 1 wrong
90 val gap = longestGap(EVENTS, "a") // 295 — the allowance must beat this
91 val saved = 0 // keys the bound saves, at any moment, at this scale
Step 6/0 — then the next "a" event arrives
It lands at 540, finds no accumulator for "a", and starts one — **because a key dropped a moment ago is indistinguishable from a key never seen.** The order in
`onEvent` is drop-then-add, and no ordering fixes this: the information that would distinguish the two cases is exactly the information that was deleted.
